meta.title: Pensions into Inheritance Tax from April 2027: Impact Model

sources.name: Inheritance Tax on unused pension funds and death benefits (policy paper / tax information and impact note), HM Revenue & Customs, published 21 July 2025
Inheritance Tax on pensions: liability, reporting and payment (technical consultation, 30 October 2024 to 22 January 2025; outcome published 21 July 2025), HMRC
Inheritance Tax on pensions: liability, reporting and payment - summary of responses, HMRC, 21 July 2025
Inheritance Tax liabilities statistics: commentary, HMRC accredited official statistics, updated 31 July 2025 (data to tax year 2022 to 2023)

policy.what_changes: From 6 April 2027 most unused pension funds and death benefits payable from registered pension schemes are included in the value of a person's estate for Inheritance Tax. Personal representatives, not pension scheme administrators, are liable for reporting and paying the tax (a reversal of the original consultation proposal). A new scheme will let beneficiaries direct pension scheme administrators to pay the Inheritance Tax on their behalf directly to HMRC.
in_scope: Unused defined contribution pension funds (drawdown and uncrystallised pots) remaining at death
Most lump sum death benefits payable from registered pension schemes
out_of_scope: All death in service benefits payable from a registered pension scheme, whether the scheme is discretionary or non-discretionary (consultation response, 21 July 2025)
Dependants' scheme pensions from a defined benefit arrangement or a collective money purchase arrangement (policy paper, 21 July 2025)

Benefits passing to a surviving spouse or civil partner: the existing spouse/civil partner exemption applies, including survivor payments under a joint life annuity where the survivor is a spouse or civil partner
Benefits passing to registered charities: existing charity exemption maintained
policy.liability_mechanics: Personal representatives are liable for reporting and payment from 6 April 2027. Exempt beneficiaries (including spouses and civil partners) can take their benefits immediately. Per the July 2025 policy paper, personal representatives can direct pension scheme administrators to withhold 50% of the taxable benefits for up to 15 months from the date of death, or pay the Inheritance Tax due to HMRC before releasing the remainder to pension beneficiaries.
policy.stated_rationale: HMRC states pension schemes were increasingly used and marketed as a tax planning vehicle to transfer wealth rather than for funding retirement, and the change removes inconsistencies in the Inheritance Tax treatment of different types of pensions.

context_series.note: HMRC accredited official statistics; taxpaying estates and total IHT liabilities by tax year of wealth transfer. 2020-21 estates count not published in the commentary extract used; null = not verified, not zero.

worked_model.disclaimer: Illustrations only. Computed arithmetically from the stated 2026/27 rules and assumptions below; they are not statistics and not advice. Assumes nil rate band £325,000, residence nil rate band £175,000 (home passing to direct descendants), RNRB tapered by £1 for every £2 the estate exceeds £2,000,000, IHT rate 40%, no other reliefs or exemptions, and that thresholds are unchanged at the relevant date.

scenarios.label: Estate of £500,000 plus £300,000 unused pension pot, home to children
scenarios.note: Newly liable: pays nothing today, £120,000 from April 2027.

scenarios.label: Estate of £900,000 plus £400,000 pension, home to children
scenarios.note: Already taxpaying; extra £160,000, exactly 40% of the pension.

scenarios.label: Estate of £1,800,000 plus £500,000 pension: RNRB taper case
scenarios.note: Pension pushes the estate to £2,300,000, so RNRB is tapered from £175,000 to £25,000. Extra IHT £260,000 on a £500,000 pension: £200,000 taxed at 40% and the £300,000 slice above £2,000,000 at an effective 60% marginal rate (40% plus the RNRB clawback).

scenarios.label: Widowed person, estate £1,000,000 plus £600,000 pension, full transferred allowances
scenarios.note: Doubled NRB and RNRB via transferable allowances (£650,000 plus £350,000). No IHT today; £240,000 from April 2027.
